papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Single-Channel Surface EMG Classification for Low-Resource Hand Gesture Recognition: A Subject-Independent Evaluation
papers.abstract: Abstract Single-channel surface electromyography (sEMG) could reduce the cost and complexity of hand-gesture interfaces, but performance commonly degrades when models are tested on unseen subjects. We evaluated five-class hand gesture classification using only the Flexor Carpi Radialis (FCR) channel from 83 quality-screened subjects drawn from 113 recordings. Time-domain (TD) features were classified with multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) and three uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods: Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout, Deep Ensembles, and Evidential Deep Learning (EDL). A raw-window one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) and a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) were included as end-to-end comparators. The best within-subject result was obtained by Random Forest at $$73.3\%\pm 13.3\%$$ , while full-coverage leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOSOCV) accuracy was $$51.1\%\pm 10.3\%$$ for the MLP baseline; all UQ methods were statistically indistinguishable from this baseline after Holm correction. Confidence-based selective prediction improved per-subject accuracy to $$68.3\%$$ at $$50\%$$ coverage and $$83.9\%$$ at $$30\%$$ coverage, but this gain was achieved equally by plain MLP softmax confidence and by MC Dropout, indicating that the improvement arises from the confidence-ordering property of softmax outputs rather than from stochastic inference. The deterministic MLP achieved the best calibration (Expected Calibration Error, ECE $$=0.024$$ ), while EDL showed vacuity collapse and was the only method to degrade under selective prediction (ECE $$=0.341$$ ). Both 1D-CNN and TCN showed numerically lower LOSOCV accuracy than the TD+MLP pipeline under the evaluated preprocessing configuration, though the differences were not statistically significant after Holm correction; loss of amplitude information through per-sample normalisation is a plausible contributing factor. Per-class analysis revealed that selective prediction gains are structurally concentrated in the rest class, which is retained at $$97.5\%$$ coverage with near-perfect accuracy ( $$99.7\%$$ ); excluding rest, active-gesture accuracy at $$50\%$$ coverage was only $$46.5\%$$ . This rest-class dominance effect has direct implications for how selective prediction should be evaluated in sEMG datasets that include a rest class. External validation on NinaPro DB2 (40 subjects, one circumferential forearm channel) confirmed above-chance classification ( $$p<0.0001$$ ) but showed no meaningful correlation between uncertainty and per-subject accuracy ( $$r=+0.047$$ ), indicating that the UQ mechanism does not generalise to this dataset. These results indicate that standard softmax confidence, requiring no additional training or inference overhead, is sufficient for rejection-based low-resource sEMG deployment under the evaluated conditions; computationally expensive stochastic inference methods provide no measurable additional benefit on low-dimensional tabular features.

papers.title: A physics-informed neural network-based computational method for forward and inverse analysis of buried pipelines subjected to lateral landslides
papers.abstract: Buried oil and gas pipelines in mountainous regions are frequently subjected to transverse landslide loading, necessitating accurate forward mechanical prediction and reliable inverse load identification for structural safety evaluation. Conventional finite element methods serve as the standard tool for forward analysis of such structures, yet they inherently lack the capability to assimilate sparse field monitoring data—a critical prerequisite for quantifying unknown landslide-induced loads. Although physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) offer unified forward–inverse modeling capacity, their practical application to large-scale pipeline problems is limited by inherent spectral bias, stringent strong-form continuity requirements, and automatic differentiation overhead. This study proposes a domain-decomposed energy-based PINN framework for Winkler-supported pipeline beams, adopting single-hidden-layer networks with cubic Hermite interpolation, analytical differentiation, and a weak-form energy loss functional. The established framework supports both single-stage static load identification via bilevel optimization and Tikhonov regularization, as well as two-stage time-varying load evolution tracking through dual-network temporal coupling. Benefiting from the unified PINN architecture, heterogeneous monitoring data including deflection, rotation, and strain measurements can be flexibly fused across staged monitoring procedures. Forward validation against ABAQUS benchmarks under both cosine and asymmetric ridge load distributions yields relative errors below 0.2% for deflection, rotation, bending moment, and strain. Inverse tests for both load patterns demonstrate that deflection-based monitoring achieves high-accuracy load reconstruction (RMSE <80 kN / m ) with five or more sensors, and two-stage incremental monitoring effectively refines time-varying load amplitude estimation, albeit constrained by the baseline accuracy of initial sparse inversion. Further validation with 5% peak-amplitude Gaussian noise shows that the load identification accuracy and the inherent sensitivity hierarchy of structural responses are well preserved, demonstrating the favorable noise robustness and reliability of the proposed framework. This work presents an accurate, robust, and efficient physics-informed paradigm for geohazard monitoring and safety assessment of buried pipeline infrastructures.

papers.title: Femoral Head Osteochondral Lesions Predict Lower Survivorship but Not Inferior Patient‐Reported Outcomes After Hip Arthroscopy at a Minimum 10‐Year Follow‐Up
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the long-term outcomes of patients undergoing hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome and labral tears who were found to have femoral head (FH) cartilage lesions and to compare these results to a matched control group of patients without FH cartilage damage. METHODS: Prospectively collected data were retrospectively reviewed for patients who underwent primary hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome and labral tears between February 2008 and April 2014. Patients were included if they had completed preoperative questionnaires, with follow-up defined as having minimum 10-year postoperative patient-reported outcomes or a documented endpoint. Patients with Tönnis grade >1 were excluded. Patients with FH osteochondral lesions (Outerbridge grade ≥2) were propensity matched 1:1 to controls without FH damage based on age, sex, body mass index, lateral center-edge angle, labral treatment, capsular management, acetabular Outerbridge, and follow-up time. Clinically relevant thresholds, survivorship, and predictors of conversion to arthroplasty were included in the analysis. RESULTS: A total of 188 patients (94 per group) were included. The FH group showed comparable improvements in all evaluated patient-reported outcomes compared with the control group at the latest follow-up (P < .01), with both groups achieving the minimal clinically important thresholds at similar rates. The FH lesion group had a significantly higher rate of conversion to total hip arthroplasty (23.4% vs 11.7%, P = .03). Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression identified increasing FH damage severity as an independent predictor of conversion (hazard ratio 3.9, 95% confidence interval 1.73-9.13, P = .001). CONCLUSIONS: Patients who underwent hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome and labral tears with concomitant FH osteochondral lesions showed significant functional improvements comparable to those of a matched control group at long-term follow-up. However, their higher conversion rate to arthroplasty supported by regression analysis highlights FH damage as a key determinant of long-term survivorship after hip arthroscopy. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, retrospective cohort study.

papers.title: Surgical site infection and associated risk factors in elderly patients undergoing hip arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Fracture of the femoral neck, prevalent among the elderly, is typically managed through total hip arthroplasty or hemiarthroplasty. In this demographic, there is an increased risk of surgical site infections (SSIs), contributing to extended hospital stays, increased morbidity, and mortality. This study aims to determine the incidence rate of SSIs following hip surgery in the elderly and to identify associated risk factors. A comprehensive search of MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library was conducted for relevant studies published up to May 2024. Observational studies reporting the incidence rate of SSIs and associated risk factors were included in this analysis. The primary outcome was the incidence rate of SSIs post-hip surgery, along with potential risk factors. This study is registered with PROSPERO (ID: CRD42024583178) and adheres to the PRISMA guidelines. Seven studies were included in the analysis. The pooled incidence rate of hip SSIs was 1.98% (95% CI: 0.96-4.11). Analysis of risk factors revealed that patients with a BMI≥35 had a significantly increased risk of SSIs in the hip joint [OR 4.01 (95% CI: 2.55-6.31)]. However, the pooled analysis indicated that diabetes mellitus [OR 1.65 (95% CI: 0.80-3.39)] and age≥67 years [OR 1.85 (95% CI: 0.29-11.75)] were not significantly associated with an increased risk of hip SSIs. Our study concludes that obesity is a significant risk factor for the development of surgical site infections in elderly patients following hip surgery.

papers.title: Prosthodontic Determinants of Peri-Implant Tissue Health: A Narrative Review
papers.abstract: Peri-implant tissue health is a critical determinant of long-term implant success and patient satisfaction. While osseointegration remains the biologic foundation of implant dentistry, prosthodontic factors significantly influence the maintenance of peri-implant hard and soft tissues. Contemporary evidence suggests that restoration design, implant-abutment connection, emergence profile, retention type, occlusal loading, restorative material, and maintenance protocols collectively affect the incidence of peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis. This review summarizes current evidence regarding prosthodontic considerations that contribute to peri-implant tissue stability and discusses contemporary strategies to minimize biologic and mechanical complications. Special emphasis is placed on emergence profile design, cement excess, prosthetic contours, occlusal overload, restorative material selection, and maintenance therapy. Understanding these factors enables clinicians to optimize peri-implant health and improve long-term treatment outcomes. [1–5]

papers.title: Machine learning-based inverse method for determining elastic coefficients of unsymmetric laminates
papers.abstract: Determination of equivalent elastic coefficients in composite laminates is a fundamental problem in structural mechanics and materials engineering. This task becomes particularly challenging for unsymmetric laminates, where coupling effects between membrane, bending, and shear responses render analytical characterisation difficult and computationally expensive. In this work, a machine learning-based inverse methodology is proposed for determining the equivalent shear modulus of unsymmetric composite laminates. A high-fidelity finite element implementation of the ASTM V-notched shear test is used to generate a comprehensive dataset covering a wide range of unsymmetric stacking sequences. A Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) model is trained as a nonlinear surrogate to map laminate design variables to the corresponding equivalent shear modulus. The trained model is subsequently employed in an inverse design framework to identify laminate stacking sequences that achieve prescribed target values of shear modulus. The proposed approach significantly reduces computational cost compared to conventional trial-and-error finite element analysis and provides new insight into the relationship between laminate architecture and effective shear behaviour.

papers.title: Advanced Bioactive and Regenerative Scaffolds for Early Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head: From Bone Regeneration to Functional Recovery
papers.abstract: Osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) is a progressive disorder characterized by impaired vascular supply, dysregulated bone remodeling, and loss of structural integrity that may ultimately lead to femoral-head collapse and total hip arthroplasty. This narrative review aimed to critically examine advanced bioactive and regenerative scaffold strategies for early-stage ONFH, with emphasis on biomaterial design, osteogenesis–angiogenesis coupling, microenvironment modulation, clinical translation, and functional recovery. A structured literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted from database inception to 14 August 2026, and relevant preclinical and clinical studies were synthesized qualitatively. Preclinical evidence demonstrates progressive development from osteoconductive matrices toward functionally graded, cell-assisted, bioactive-ion, oxygen-releasing, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory platforms, supporting biological plausibility and technological feasibility. In contrast, clinical evidence remains limited, heterogeneous, and predominantly observational or open-label. No randomized controlled trial specifically evaluating an advanced regenerative scaffold platform was identified among the studies included in this review. Advanced regenerative scaffolds therefore represent promising joint-preserving strategies, but their clinical value remains to be established through reproducible scaffold characterization, appropriate patient and lesion selection, standardized outcomes, long-term native-hip survival assessment, and well-designed comparative studies.

papers.title: Association between cemented and uncemented cups and risk of revision in patients aged 65 years or older following primary total hip arthroplasty: a study of 310,515 patients from the Nordic Arthroplasty Register Association
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Cemented stem fixation in total hip arthroplasty (THA) reduces early femoral fracture risk in elderly patients, but the optimal method of cup fixation remains controversial. We aimed to compare cup revision risk between cemented and uncemented acetabular cups in patients aged 65 years or older undergoing primary THA. METHODS: This registry-based cohort study used data from the Nordic Arthroplasty Register Association (NARA). We included patients aged 65 years or older who underwent primary THA for primary osteoarthritis or sequelae of childhood hip disorders between 1995 and 2018. The primary outcome was all-cause cup revision, with prespecified analyses stratified by age and sex. Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, femoral head size, time period, and nation was used. Follow-up was divided into 3 periods: 0-1, 1-6, and 6-26 years. RESULTS: Among 310,515 patients, cemented cups were associated with a lower risk of all-cause cup revision during the first year (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.47, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.41-0.53) and a higher risk at 6-26 years (aHR 1.91, CI 1.72-2.13). In patients aged 80 years or older, the sex-specific adjusted hazard ratios after the first year were close to 1, with wide confidence intervals. CONCLUSION: Cemented cups were associated with a lower risk of cup revision during the first year across all age groups and a higher risk at 6-26 years in the overall cohort. Among patients aged 80 years or older, we found no evidence of an association between fixation method and cup revision after the first year.

papers.title: High-centre total hip arthroplasty with acetabular augment for massive acetabular bone loss following two-stage management of an infected, chondrolysed hip after fracture-dislocation of the acetabulum: a case report
papers.abstract: Post-traumatic septic arthritis of the hip following surgical fixation of an acetabular fracture is an uncommon but devastating complication that can progress to rapid chondrolysis of the femoral head and, if unchecked, massive acetabular bone loss. Management requires a staged strategy combining infection eradication with later reconstruction. We report a 55-year-old man who sustained a traumatic hip fracture-dislocation with an undisplaced acetabular fracture, initially treated elsewhere with closed reduction followed by open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) with plating. Three months later he presented with a discharging sinus at the surgical site and radiographic evidence of near-total chondrolysis of the femoral head. He was managed with implant removal, thorough debridement and insertion of antibiotic-loaded cement beads (Girdlestone-type resection arthroplasty), followed by culture-directed systemic antibiotics. Although the infection resolved and the wound healed, the patient remained symptomatic with persistent hip pain. Repeat imaging showed complete loss of the femoral head, proximal femoral migration and near-total acetabular bone loss, confirmed on computed tomography. He subsequently underwent total hip arthroplasty (THA) with a high hip centre construct and an acetabular augment to compensate for the posterior and superior acetabular defect encountered intraoperatively. A staged protocol of aggressive debridement and antibiotic cement spacing, followed by high hip centre THA with augment support, is a viable salvage strategy for infected, chondrolysed hips with severe acetabular bone loss, and can restore a functional, pain-free joint when anatomic reconstruction is not feasible.

papers.title: Research on the energy absorption performance of diamond structures with axial and transverse porosity gradients under different load-bearing angles
papers.abstract: Background In biomedical, aerospace, automotive and marine engineering, there is an increasing demand for high energy absorption behaviour in structures. Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures, such as Diamond lattices, have emerged as promising solutions due to their light weight nature and excellent energy absorption performance, and thus they have attracted significant research interest. Methods This study explores the energy absorption characteristics and deformation behavior of Diamond structures with varying porosity distributions under different loading angles. Uniform and gradient Diamond structures with axial and transverse porosity distributions were generated. Quasi-static compression tests were performed on the uniform structures, while FE simulations were used to investigate the mechanical and energy-absorption responses of the uniform and gradient configurations. Quasi-static compression tests and finite element (FE) simulations were used to analyze the changes in energy absorption characteristics and deformation/damage modes during the compression process. Results The results show that loading orientation and porosity-gradient direction strongly influence the energy-absorption response of Diamond structures. For the uniform structure, the SEA increased to approximately 8 kJ/kg at a loading angle of 30°, representing an increase of about 33% compared with the 0° and 15° configurations, while the corresponding plateau stress reached approximately 105 MPa. When the loading angle increased to 45°, the SEA decreased to approximately 4 kJ/kg because of earlier densification. Axial-gradient structures exhibited increased plateau stress and slightly enhanced SEA, but their maximum energy-absorption efficiency remained below approximately 35%, compared with about 40% for the uniform structures. Transverse-gradient structures showed plateau stresses comparable to those of the uniform structure with the corresponding average porosity, but tended to densify earlier, resulting in reduced SEA. Conclusion These findings provide valuable insights into the design and optimization of Diamond structures for improved energy-absorption performance under different loading conditions and offer mechanical design guidance that may be relevant to the future development of TPMS structures for biomedical applications.

papers.title: Polysaccharide Bioinks for 3D Bioprinting: A Guide to Translation
papers.abstract: Polysaccharide-based hydrogels offer versatile platforms for three-dimensional bioprinting, but translation requires coordinated assessment of formulation, processing, and biological performance. This narrative review connects backbone chemistry and functionalization with rheology, crosslinking, printing modality, cellular responses, and manufacturing requirements. It examines alginate, hyaluronic acid, chitosan, cellulose derivatives, gellan gum, and complementary polysaccharides, distinguishing cell-laden bioinks from acellular biomaterial inks and supporting materials. A study-specific framework separates material feasibility, cell-laden printing, functional in vitro outcomes, preclinical evaluation, and preliminary human feasibility without assigning maturity scores to entire material families. Print fidelity and cellular remodeling impose competing requirements whose balance is formulation- and application-dependent. Dual or sequential crosslinking, dynamic networks, and support-bath printing provide complementary approaches rather than a universal solution. Inconsistent reporting limits cross-study comparison; a minimum reporting set is therefore proposed. Sterilization, raw-material variability, quality control, long-term safety, and regulatory classification are considered alongside formulation design. Future priorities include tissue-appropriate viscoelasticity, granular architectures, hierarchical vascularization, and reproducible data-driven optimization. Clinical translation will require stronger links between manufacturing reproducibility and sustained biological function, rather than printing accuracy alone.

papers.title: Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells as a Promising Path Toward Zone-Specific Meniscus Regeneration
papers.abstract: For young and middle-aged patients with irreparable meniscal tears, preserving or restoring meniscal tissue is critical to maintaining joint function and delaying osteoarthritis. Yet, when repair is not feasible, partial meniscectomy remains common and can compromise the load-bearing function of the knee, underscoring a highly unmet medical need for regenerative strategies that restore functional tissue rather than simply relieve symptoms. Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) offer a scalable and potentially patient-matched source of progenitor cells for meniscal regeneration, with iPSC-derived cartilage already entering clinical study for articular cartilage defects. However, translating this progress to the meniscus presents a fundamental biological challenge: restoring a specialized, zonally organized tissue rather than simply generating sufficient cells. The meniscus is a structurally, mechanically, and biologically graded tissue with distinct inner, transitional, and outer zones. Consequently, generating fibrocartilage is unlikely to reproduce native meniscal function. In this review, we examine iPSC-based strategies through the framework of zone-specific meniscal regeneration, focusing on meniscal fibrochondrocyte generation and reconstruction of native tissue architecture. We compare biofabrication strategies against native structural, vascular, and mechanical benchmarks, and outline the preclinical, manufacturing and regulatory requirements for translating iPSC-derived meniscal constructs toward patient-centered clinical application.

papers.title: Functional outcome of non-cemented total hip arthroplasty for avascular necrosis in adults of below 50 years age group
papers.abstract: Background: Avascular necrosis (AVN) of the femoral head is a progressive disorder causing joint destruction and functional impairment, particularly in younger adults. Total hip arthroplasty (THA) is the standard treatment for advanced AVN and non-cemented prostheses are increasingly preferred because of their biomechanical advantages and long-term stability. This study evaluated the functional outcomes of non-cemented THA in AVN patients under 50 years of age. Methods: A prospective observational study was conducted at the National Institute of Traumatology and Orthopaedic Rehabilitation (NITOR), Dhaka, Bangladesh, from September 2021 to March 2024. Thirty-four patients with late-stage AVN (Ficat & Arlet Stage III and IV) underwent non-cemented THA. Functional outcomes were assessed preoperatively and postoperatively using the Harris Hip Score (HHS), range of motion (ROM), pain severity, walking distance and need for support. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 25, with p<0.05 considered statistically significant. Results: The mean age was 35.50±7.01 years and 73.53% were male. Mean HHS improved significantly from 37.12 preoperatively to 91.44 postoperatively (p=0.001), with 61.8% achieving excellent outcomes (HHS >90). Significant improvements were observed in pain severity, limping, support dependency and walking distance (p=0.001). ROM also improved significantly, with 64.71% achieving a postoperative ROM of 161°–210°. Complications were minimal, including superficial surgical site infection in 5.88% and limb length discrepancy in 2.94%. Conclusions: Non-cemented THA provides significant pain relief and improvement in mobility, ROM and functional outcomes in AVN patients under 50 years, with minimal complications, supporting its use in younger active patients.

papers.title: A Physics-Informed Surrogate Safety Gate for Agentic AI Control of SMT Reflow Soldering in Unmanned-System Electronics Manufacturing: A Simulation-Based Study
papers.abstract: Surface mount technology (SMT) assembly lines running under high-mix low-volume (HMLV) conditions face a recurring parameter-optimization problem, because frequent product changeovers invalidate static control recipes and expose the nonlinear coupling between solder paste printing and reflow soldering. A large language model (LLM) can reason about that coupling. Its outputs are probabilistic and its inference latency is network-dependent, so it cannot be wired directly to process actuators. This paper takes that obstacle as its research question. The proposed multilayer Agentic AI and physics-informed digital twin (Agentic AI-DT) framework, a digital-twin architecture evaluated here as a digital model driven by a simulated closed loop, places a cloud-hosted LLM in the strategy role and an edge-deployed conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE), trained with a thermodynamic partial differential equation residual penalty, in the role of a gate that runs the same deterministic check on every strategy before it reaches the reflow oven controller. The check executes deterministically, but its verdicts inherit the surrogate's prediction error, so the safety it provides is measured here and not assumed. The study measures the gate itself: how often it fires, and how often it errs in each direction. A two-stage pipeline combining Latin Hypercube Sampling with singular value decomposition based reduced-order modelling expands 1,000 calibrated finite element simulations into 50,000 training scenarios, and 200 further independent finite element runs form the held-out test set. On those runs the physics-informed CVAE reaches a mean squared error of 1.93 ℃ 2 , 25.2% below a CVAE trained without the physics term and 14.6% below a standalone physics-informed neural network. Across 347 candidate strategies the gate vetoes 63 (18.2%). Finite element re-simulation shows that 5 of the 284 admitted candidates (1.76%, 95% CI 0.8 to 4.1%) were unsafe and that 14 of the 63 vetoed candidates (22.2%, 95% CI 13.7 to 33.9%) were safe, giving 94.5% agreement with the reference solver. Closed-loop profile tracking error is 2.09 ℃, against 3.18 ℃ for model predictive control and 4.62 ℃ for fixed-gain PID. The diagnostic layer names the injected root cause in 84.0% of 300 scripted fault trials, against 72.7% for a random forest classifier and 61.3% for a rule-based expert system. Median end-to-end latency is 419 ms, 90.7% of 2,000 cycles finish inside the 500 ms design budget, and the remaining cycles commit a re-checked last validated setpoint at the 500 ms boundary, reaching the controller within 539 ms. Every number reported here comes from a synthetic environment calibrated against three published sets of measured reflow profiles. No physical production line was instrumented, so these are simulation-fidelity measurements rather than production performance guarantees.

papers.title: Accelerating hybrid model predictive control using warm-started generalized benders decomposition
papers.abstract: Hybrid model predictive control with both continuous and discrete variables is widely applicable to robotic control tasks, especially those involving contacts with the environment. Due to combinatorial complexity, the solving speed of hybrid MPC can be insufficient for real-time applications. In this paper, we propose a hybrid MPC algorithm based on Generalized Benders Decomposition. The algorithm enumerates and stores cutting planes online inside a finite buffer and transfers them across MPC iterations to provide warm-starts for new problem instances, significantly enhancing solving speed. We theoretically analyze this warm-starting performance by modeling the deviation of mode sequences through temporal shifting and stretching, deriving bounds on the dual gap between transferred optimality cuts and the true optimal costs, and utilizing these bounds to quantify the level of suboptimality guaranteed in the first solve of the Benders Master Problem. Our algorithm is validated in simulation through controlling a cart-pole system with soft contact walls, a free-flying robot navigating around obstacles, and a humanoid robot standing on one leg while pushing against walls with its hands for balance. For our benchmark problems, the algorithm enumerates cuts on the order of only tens to hundreds while reaching speeds 2-3 times faster than the off-the-shelf solver Gurobi, oftentimes exceeding 1000 Hz. The code is available at https://github.com/XuanLin/Benders-MPC.

papers.title: Accuracy and Computational Cost of Standard and Sequential Time-Window Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Transient Heat Conduction with a Moving Gaussian Heat Source
papers.abstract: Background The thermal field generated by a moving laser heat source evolves continuously as the laser scans across a material surface. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) offer an alternative for modeling transient heat transfer, but quantitative comparisons between full-domain and sequential time-window training remain limited. Methods This study compares Standard PINN and Sequential Time-Window PINN for two-dimensional transient heat conduction with a moving Gaussian heat source at scanning speeds of 1, 2, and 3 mms−1 over 10 s. Reference solutions were obtained using the forward-time central-space (FTCS) method on a 500×500 grid after grid-convergence and stability checks. Standard PINN was trained over the full temporal domain, whereas Sequential Time-Window PINN used ten consecutive 1 s windows with parameter transfer between windows. Results Standard PINN achieved a maximum-temperature mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.461–0.619 °C and a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.210−0.322% . Sequential Time-Window PINN yielded a maximum-temperature MAE of 19.248−25.581°C . Its absolute errors ranged from 103.05 to 158.16 °C at 1 s and decreased to 0.98−6.64°C at 10 s. Sequential Time-Window PINN trained 6.80−7.89 times faster than Standard PINN. However, both PINN approaches required more computational time than FTCS. Conclusions Standard PINN provided higher predictive accuracy, whereas Sequential Time-Window PINN reduced training time but produced larger errors, particularly during the early simulation. Differences in training-point counts, collocation-point sampling, and temporal strategy prevent attributing the runtime reduction solely to time-windowing. Further controlled experiments are needed to isolate the effects of these factors on accuracy and computational cost.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Global Model Development via Federated Learning for Indoor Temperature Prediction Toward Advanced Building Control
papers.abstract: Model-based predictive control provides an effective approach for improving building energy efficiency by optimizing heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning operation while maintaining indoor thermal conditions. However, its performance strongly depends on the availability of an accurate and generalizable prediction model of building thermal dynamics. Existing studies have focused on individual buildings, where each building is modeled and optimized independently. Recent studies have demonstrated the potential of federated learning (FL) for a range of building applications. However, most existing approaches remain predominantly data driven. This study proposes a federated physics-informed neural network for generalized indoor temperature prediction across multiple building zones. The global RC model was developed and then incorporated into the neural-network loss function as a physics-based constraint, while FL was employed to develop a shared global prediction model without pooling the raw datasets of individual clients. The developed global model demonstrated good single-step-ahead prediction performance across the four target zones, with root-mean squared error (RMSE) values ranging from 0.36 °C to 0.59 °C, mean absolute error values from 0.25 °C to 0.57 °C. For multi-step-ahead prediction, the average RMSE was approximately 0.68 °C during the estimation period and 0.99 °C during validation. Moreover, when the zone excluded from the federated training process and evaluated as an unseen client the proposed model achieved RMSE values of 0.74 °C and 0.86 °C for one-step-ahead and multi-step-ahead predictions, respectively, compared with 0.86 °C and 0.98 °C for the conventional data-driven FL model.

The mixture of Al and Pb or Al and Sn powders was spread with a doctor blade onto a heated substrate and laser-irradiated to produce compact samples via LPBF. Synthesis was carried out at a constant laser scanning speed of v = 1.2 m/s and power levels ranging from 70 to 130 W. The results confirmed that the structure of the resulting aluminum composites strongly depends on the physical and thermodynamic properties of the soft alloying additive and differs significantly at equal volume concentrations. In the case of the Al-20Sn composite, it exhibits a dendritic morphology, whereas for Al-20Pb, it shows a cellular structure. Compression tests demonstrated that increasing the laser power up to 130 W enhances the plasticity of the LPBF-processed Al-20Pb composite, reaching 25%, which is substantially higher than that of the Al-20Sn alloy. Meanwhile, the ultimate compressive strength σU of both alloys was approximately equal, standing at about 100 MPa. The main failure mechanisms of the studied alloys are discussed.

papers.title: Exploring the Relationship Between Consciousness, the Human Body, and Biofabrication
papers.abstract: Consciousness is commonly discussed as the capacity to experience sensations, thoughts, emotions, intentions, and awareness of self and surroundings. The human body provides the biological structures through which many of these experiences are expressed and regulated, while the nervous system coordinates information across the organism. Biofabrication, including tissue engineering, organoid technology, and three-dimensional bioprinting, approaches the body from another direction: it seeks to construct or restore living biological structures by combining cells, biomaterials, biological signals, and controlled fabrication methods. This project explores the conceptual relationship among these three domains without assuming that consciousness can currently be engineered or reproduced. It examines how body structure and function support conscious experience, how biofabrication attempts to reproduce selected properties of living tissues, and why reproducing biological structure is not equivalent to reproducing subjective experience. The discussion also considers neural tissue engineering, organoids, personalized medicine, ethical questions, and the technical limits of present-day biofabrication. The central theme is that consciousness, embodiment, and biofabrication can be studied together as connected but distinct scientific questions.

papers.title: A Controlled Disentanglement Protocol for Label-Efficient Fraud Detection on Drifting Transaction Graphs
papers.abstract: Label-efficient fraud detection on drifting transaction graphs has two design axes: the predictor (feature representation and model class) and the acquisition rule that chooses which cases analysts label. Active learning evaluations typically vary only the acquisition rule, so reported gains can conflate the two. We propose a controlled disentanglement protocol that separates them: a prequential closed loop with a random-acquisition floor, a full cross of predictor against acquisition rule, and pre-specified credibility criteria. Applied across three datasets, two graph constructions, and a ladder of acquisition strategies including Drift-Conditioned Active Learning (DCAL), the protocol locates the dominant lever in the predictor: tree ensembles on raw features exceed a linear head on frozen graph embeddings by +0.26 in area under the precision–recall curve (AUC-PR), a gap localized to the interaction of raw features with a nonlinear model; a single raw-feature random forest (0.704) exceeds the full committee (0.614). Once the predictor is controlled, no acquisition strategy holds a stable advantage beyond a small edge for uncertainty sampling that appears under the linear head and vanishes under the committee predictor. The effect replicates on Elliptic++ transactions (+0.173). Practitioners should invest in representation and model class, and use drift detection as a retraining trigger rather than a labeling rule.

papers.title: A Review of Machine Learning Techniques for Analog-To-Digital Converter Design Automation
papers.abstract: ADCs play an important role in converting information from the analog world to the digital one; with modern applications requiring higher resolutions, speed, and power efficiency, it has become very difficult to design them. Traditionally, the design of an ADC follows an iterative design process that includes stages like specification, behavioral modeling, transistor sizing, schematic simulation, layout, and post-layout verification, which is laborious and requires much designer expertise due to the consideration of process-voltage-temperature variations and yield. In this work, we perform a review of the latest advancements in the use of machine learning (ML) to tackle the challenges of ADC design in recent years, with systematic search from 2015 to 2026 in IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and arXiv. Rather than organizing the literature on different ML algorithms, this paper categorizes ML approaches such as regression, tree-based models, SVM, ANN, CNN, GNN, reinforcement learning, evolutionary algorithms, and Bayesian optimization in ADC design stages such as behavioral modeling, transistor sizing, calibration of comparators and capacitor arrays, calibration of ADC, layout optimization, prediction of PVT/yield variations, and design space exploration. Comparative analysis includes the benefits provided by each technique such as speed and accuracy improvements, as well as their main drawbacks. Open challenges are then presented, including lack of data, poor generalization performance, low explainability, and the largely unexplored topic of co-optimization across multiple stages. Finally, future trends in the field are presented in terms of new directions such as generative AI, GNN-based layout optimization, physics-informed learning, digital twins, and human-AI collaborative design, as well as risks and potential problems such as manufacturability and IP in generative approaches

papers.title: Epistemic Justice-Aware Checklist Learning an Adaptive and Auditable Governance Framework for Bias and Fairness in Generative AI Curriculum Design
papers.abstract: Generative AI increasingly participates in curriculum design, yet the resulting syllabi, learning outcomes, and assessments may reproduce subtle epistemic injustices that existing governance instruments fail to detect. We propose an adaptive and auditable framework that learns a bias and fairness checklist for generative AI curriculum artifacts rather than treating such a checklist as a static set of rules. The proposed method encodes curriculum texts into two disentangled latent subspaces, one capturing pedagogical utility and the other capturing epistemic justice violations, through a contrastive objective combined with intersectional adversarial debiasing. A psychometric utility-preserving penalty constrains this separation so that debiasing does not degrade instructional quality. Each checklist item is then evaluated by an evidential deep learning head that outputs a Dirichlet distribution over compliance states, hence yielding calibrated violation probabilities and explicit uncertainty estimates. An uncertainty-aware routing mechanism subsequently directs low-confidence drafts to a Faculty Expert Panel, whose decisions and justification notes are returned to a fine-tuning dataset. This feedback loop updates the checklist definitions and model weights iteratively, therefore allowing the governance instrument to adapt to newly identified forms of subtle bias. The main contribution is a mathematically grounded pipeline that couples representation disentanglement, evidential uncertainty quantification, and human expert feedback within a single auditable process. For curriculum governance, the framework offers transparent violation probabilities, traceable expert interventions, and a documented evolution of fairness criteria, which together support accountability in generative AI-assisted educational design.

papers.title: Hybrid Kalman-MPC Strategy with Detailed Case Study on Speed Control of DC Motors
papers.abstract: Abstract Effective speed control of direct current (DC) motors is often necessary for today's am industrial applications where many variables such as ambient interference, inaccurate or fluctuating parameters or changing environmental conditions may exist. Traditional control techniques such as proportional-integral-derivative (PID) control and fractional order proportional-integral-derivative (FOPID) allow for ease of implementation and low complexity. However, in dynamic and noisy environments, they may not provide optimal solution. This paper proposes a new hybrid control technique called the Kalman filter (KF) model predictive control (MPC) for speed regulation of dc motors. The Hybrid Kalman Model Predictive Controller (HKMPC) scheme uses Kalman filtering techniques to generate real-time estimated states that remove or reduce the effects of sensor noise, while the MPC will use these corrected estimated states to forecast future system behaviour and generate optimal control inputs subject to practical constraints. The HKMPC scheme is compared with traditional PID and stand-alone MPC controllers based on common performance characteristics in the time domain such as rise time, settling time, overshoot and steady state error. The simulation results, were achieved using MATLAB indicate that while the MPC improved the overall performance of the system when compared to the PID controller. The performance of the MPC degrading in a noisy environment. In contrast, the HKMPC could display improved robustness, improved speed of convergence, and improved disturbance rejection through the benefits associated with the combination of estimation and prediction of future behaviour of a system. The results show that our proposed hybrid approach strikes an optimal balance of speed, accuracy and robustness which makes it ideal for real-world applications in which measurement noise and uncertainties are present. As such, this paper highlights the potential of combining estimation and predictive control paradigms as effective next-generation control techniques for motor control applications.

papers.title: LLM-DNN Fusion for Data-Efficient Trajectory Generation in Autonomous Driving: A Hybrid Approach with MPC Optimization
papers.abstract: Autonomous vehicle (AV) trajectory planning in dense urban environments requires models that generalize to rare or previously unseen scenario types. Deep neural networks (DNNs) trained on large datasets perform poorly in such data-scarce conditions, while large language models (LLMs) generalize well but lack the numerical precision required for low-level vehicle control. This paper presents a hybrid trajectory planning framework that fuses a finetuned LLM with a multi-branch DNN at the trajectory level and applies a Model Predictive Control (MPC) controller as a final optimization stage. Gemini 1.5 Flash, fine-tuned on 479 labeled scenario-trajectory pairs, generates 15- aypoint trajectory proposals from structured textual scene descriptions. A modular DNN processes the same scene as a numerical input vector and produces a parallel trajectory proposal. The two proposals are fused by a learned trajectory refinement network, and the output is passed to an MPC controller that enforces vehicle dynamics constraints while minimizing a multi-objective cost function. Training relies on a three-step distortion- based augmentation technique, curve distortion, scale distortion, and Gaussian smoothing, that generates semi-realistic trajectory variants from a base dataset of over 70,000 labeled rows, reducing the data volume required for effective DNN training. Evaluation across 200 runs in the CARLA simulator on unseen urban scenarios shows that the MPC-enhanced hybrid model achieves an Average Displacement Error (ADE) of 0.66 m and a Final Displacement Error (FDE) of 1.94 m, corresponding to improvements of 37.7% and 34.3% over the DNN-only baseline. The collision rate (CR) decreases from 3.71% to 2.90%, a 21.8% reduction. These results establish that trajectory-level fusion of LLM semantic reasoning with DNN-based feature extraction delivers measurable accuracy and safety gains in data-efficient autonomous driving conditions. The ADE/FDE improvements are statistically significant (p < 0.001). The collision-rate reduction is a consistent trend across ablations, but it is not statistically significant at n = 200 runs (see Section 4.4).

papers.abstract: Aluminum conductor terminations are limited by an alumina film that blocks wetting and raises interfacial resistance. Existing process models absorb flux behavior into a fitted decay factor, so the composition and current schedule are tuned sequentially. Here, flux activity is resolved as a transport–reaction field whose oxide coverage feeds back to the contact resistance, closing the electro-thermal activity loop. An activity–melting synchronization index (AMSI) combining temporal overlap with precedence of film removal over liquid formation is imposed as an explicit constraint. Composition simplexes are mapped to isometric log-ratio coordinates and the segmented waveform to a bounded recursive amplitude map, so the cycle-time budget and slew limit hold structurally without repair or penalty. A coupling-aware multi-fidelity Bayesian optimizer (CAMBO) reads cross-block curvature from a three-level autoregressive surrogate to switch between joint and alternating search, and measured dynamic resistance is assimilated by an unscented Kalman filter. The optimizer reaches the target hypervolume with 26% fewer evaluations at a fully feasible search, and the selected design gains 16.9% shear strength with 13.3% less energy than the incumbent. Equal-heat trials confirm that timing governs strength.

papers.abstract: This study examines the strategies employed by school principals in improving teacher performance to create quality learning processes at State Senior High Schools (SMA Negeri) in Simeulue Regency, Aceh Province. Simeulue is a remote island district categorized as a 3T (Tertinggal, Terdepan, Terluar) region, presenting unique educational challenges including geographic isolation, limited educational infrastructure, and difficulties in teacher recruitment and retention. Using a qualitative descriptive multiple case study design, this research was conducted across three schools: SMAN 2, SMAN 3, and SMAN 4 Simeulue. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observation, and documentation involving 12 informants comprising principals, vice-principals, teachers, and education staff. Data analysis employed the Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña interactive model with NVivo 12 Plus software, and validity was established through Lincoln and Guba's trustworthiness criteria. The findings reveal that principals in Simeulue apply five key strategies: (1) transformational leadership through vision-based motivation; (2) academic supervision using clinical and collegial approaches; (3) professional development through training, worKShop facilitation, and PKB programs; (4) school culture development that fosters collaboration and discipline; and (5) utilization of Kurikulum Merdeka policy frameworKS to enhance learning innovation. These strategies collectively demonstrate significant positive impacts on teacher performance indicators and the quality of differentiated and active learning processes across the three schools. The study contributes a contextually relevant leadership model for remote island school settings in Indonesia.

papers.title: Flame response inference from pressure-only data via physics-informed neural networks
papers.abstract: This study presents a physics-informed neural network framework to reconstruct spatio-temporal acoustic pressure fields and hidden quantities—namely, velocity and heat-release-rate fluctuations—in axial combustors using only sparse pressure measurements. By embedding the linearized Euler equations into the training process, the network simultaneously enforces physical consistency and fits limited experimental data, enabling identification of the flame response. The methodology is validated across progressively more complex configurations, from canonical one-dimensional problems to quasi-one-dimensional ducts with geometric discontinuities, using high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics datasets. A two-stage training strategy, incorporating tailored activation functions and physics-based constraints, enhances robustness in flame response prediction. The framework accurately reconstructs acoustic fields, infers heat-release fluctuations, and captures flame dynamics across relevant frequency ranges. These results demonstrate the potential of physics-informed neural networks to bridge the gap between limited measurements and comprehensive thermoacoustic characterization.

papers.abstract: Within interior architecture education, anthropometry and ergonomics constitute foundational domains of knowledge for understanding the relationship between users and designed environments. Their pedagogical application often positions the user as a body to be measured, proportioned, and accommodated within space. This study recasts that initial framing by asking how these domains can be taught beyond the normative body and how they may support a relational understanding of user, action, object, and space. The study was conducted as part of an undergraduate course, Ergonomics in Interior Architecture, at Özyeğin University during the Fall 2024–2025 semester; through an active learning exercise structured around role-playing, a case study, and a poster session. The study was conducted in the Ergonomics in Interior Architecture course at Özyeğin University during the Fall 2024–2025 semester through an active learning exercise structured around role-playing, a case study, and a poster session. Students created fictional users with non-normative bodies, mapped their daily routines, and developed spatial and furniture proposals responsive to their abilities, limitations, and needs. The research material comprised the project posters and written reflections of 10 students who completed all stages of the exercise. The data were analyzed using qualitative content analysis. The findings indicate that the students moved beyond the procedural application of anthropometric and ergonomic standards, interpreting bodily difference as a generator of design reasoning. The study suggests that by centering a non-normative user in a design problem, anthropometry and ergonomics can move beyond their conventional role as instruments of fit and become pedagogical means through which students learn to understand interior space as a relational field.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Modeling of Transient Pulsating Microchannel Flow with Heat-Transfer and Entropy-Generation Trade-Off Analysis
papers.abstract: Pulsating flow offers a practical means of modifying convective heat transfer in microchannels, but thermal enhancement may be accompanied by increased thermodynamic irreversibility. This study develops a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework that couples transient thermo-fluid prediction with concurrent heat-transfer and entropy-generation assessment, rather than considering heat transfer alone. The continuity, momentum, and energy equations are embedded directly into the training process, with residual-based adaptive refinement used to improve solution resolution in high-residual regions. Independent verification of the steady reference solution gives relative discrepancies of 0.04% for the velocity profile against the analytical fully developed parabolic reference, 0.08% for the temperature profile against the finite-difference benchmark, and 3.51% for the downstream Nusselt number against the finite-difference benchmark. For the representative pulsating condition, the phase-resolved Nusselt number decreases from 5.0435 to 4.5413 (9.96%), while total entropy generation increases by 11.16% over the examined phases. The completed 27-case parameter sweep reveals a non-monotonic dependence on pulsation amplitude and frequency, indicating that stronger pulsation does not necessarily produce greater heat-transfer enhancement. Within the investigated parameter space, the condition A=0.2, f=20 Hz, and ϕ1=ϕ2=0.015 gives the highest mean Nusselt number of 7.1126, together with the lowest total entropy generation of 2.7496×10−4 W/K among the evaluated cases. These results demonstrate a physics-constrained framework for jointly evaluating thermal performance and thermodynamic cost, providing a more comprehensive basis for assessing pulsation conditions than heat-transfer enhancement alone.

papers.title: Machine Learning Algorithms for High-Resolution Gravity Prediction
papers.abstract: Namibia’s reliance on the coarse-resolution EGM2008 global geopotential model results in height conversion errors often above one meter, especially due to the lack of high-resolution terrestrial gravity data. This research analyzes Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), and Universal Kriging for the creation of high-resolution Bouguer gravity anomaly grids in the Khomas Region of Namibia. The study utilized 125 terrestrial gravity observations from the Bureau Gravimétrique International (BGI), along with SRTM elevation data and lithological density values, to train and test the models at spatial resolutions of 1.86 km and 9.26 km. Spatially Distributed Hold-Out Validation (SDHV) technique was used to check how accurate the model performed. GPR returned the best indicative accuracy (MAE = 4.67 mGal; RMSE = 5.33 mGal) and strongest agreement with Universal Kriging (r = 0.9073), while ANN exhibited overfitting tendencies at fine spatial scales and SVM produced the most conservative resolution-invariant outputs. All four techniques consistently replicated the prevailing northwest–southeast regional gravity gradient, with model divergence limited to short-wavelength spatial detail. These results show that machine learning may be used to simulate regional gravity fields and give a methodological framework to help with geoid refining and updating vertical datums in Namibia.

papers.title: Fairness-Constrained Distributionally Robust Causal Policy Optimization for Adaptive Instruction in Higher Education
papers.abstract: Adaptive instructional policies in higher education often optimize short-term engagement at the expense of durable learning gains, and they frequently neglect heterogeneity across student subpopulations. We propose a fairness-constrained distributionally robust causal policy optimization framework that replaces standard deep reinforcement learning agents with a causally grounded decision-making pipeline. A structural causal model of the educational environment is constructed first, and doubly robust estimation is then applied to observational log data so that confounding bias in the counterfactual evaluation of instructional actions is mitigated. To guard against distribution shifts and adversarial perturbations in student populations, the policy optimization problem is formulated as a distributionally robust objective that maximizes worst-case expected utility over an ambiguity set centered on the empirical distribution. The policy itself is represented by reduced-rank policy trees, which preserve interpretability while remaining computationally tractable, and multi-objective Bayesian optimization is employed to balance average performance, cross-subgroup variance, and explicit disparity constraints. Fairness is enforced through Lagrangian relaxation, while causal effect decomposition separates direct instructional effects from those mediated by motivation or cognitive load. Periodic off-policy evaluation and counterfactual subgroup audits provide closed-loop validation, triggering retraining or constraint tightening when inequities emerge. The main contribution is an integrated methodology that unites causal inference, distributional robustness, and subgroup fairness within a single policy learning loop for higher education. This approach is significant because it offers a principled path toward instructional policies that remain effective, equitable, and auditable throughout their deployment lifecycle.

papers.title: Infrastructure-Aware Materials Discovery: Resource Allocation, Cost, and Carbon in AI-Driven Workflows
papers.abstract: Abstract Machine-learned interatomic potentials have converted materials-discovery campaigns from tens to hundreds of expensive density-functional calculations into populations of 10^4 to 10^6 short, independent evaluations, relocating the dominant constraint from the electronic-structure solver to the orchestration layer beneath it. We organize AI-driven materials-discovery workloads into four recurring classes—short independent screening tasks, long-running simulations, tightly coupled ab initio calculations, and iterative active-learning loops—and map spot and preemptible computing, checkpointing and workflow-level fault tolerance, autoscaling, cloud bursting, cost-aware Bayesian optimization, and carbon-aware scheduling against this taxonomy. High-throughput screening of metal–organic frameworks serves as a case study arguing that the optimal balance of elastic, stable, and interruptible resources follows from task duration, computational coupling, and recovery cost rather than from generic cloud-optimization heuristics. We further argue that the realized cost of a materials calculation decomposes into scientific, provisioning, recovery, and data-movement terms, of which only the first is a property of the calculation itself. Because the remaining terms vary with market and grid conditions on timescales of minutes, an acquisition function that prices candidates by fidelity alone systematically misprices the campaign it is scheduling. Integrating infrastructure cost and carbon signals into scientific decision-making is identified as a key open problem for autonomous discovery.

papers.title: Review of Applications of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) in Water Resource Engineering
papers.abstract: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) have evolved from primarily cartographic and spatial-data management environments into core analytical infrastructure for water-resource engineering. Their application now spans watershed delineation, rainfall–runoff modelling, groundwater assessment, flood and drought analysis, irrigation planning, water-quality assessment, river management and water-distribution infrastructure. However, the literature is fragmented across application domains and frequently attributes the predictive capability of remote sensing, hydrological models or machine-learning algorithms to GIS itself. This review critically synthesizes the evidence contained in a 20-study working corpus and supplements it with recent peer-reviewed literature to identify how GIS contributes to water-resource engineering, where its contribution is strongest, and which methodological weaknesses continue to limit transferability and decision reliability. The review is organized around six application domains and evaluates the GIS role across data integration, terrain analysis, spatial modelling, decision support, visualization and model coupling. The synthesis shows a transition from conventional GIS-based watershed and groundwater mapping toward integrated workflows combining digital elevation models, satellite observations, hydrological/hydraulic models, geostatistics, artificial intelligence and cloud computing. Nevertheless, recurring weaknesses are evident: non-reproducible literature selection, inconsistent validation, inadequate uncertainty quantification, scale mismatch, dependence on subjective weighting in multi-criteria methods, insufficient benchmarking between GIS-enabled and non-GIS workflows, and geographical concentration of evidence.Recent systematic reviews reinforce these concerns, particularly the need for standardized validation and uncertainty protocols and for multi-source, physically informed modelling. The review therefore proposes a GIS–water-resource engineering framework in which GIS is treated not as the predictive model itself but as the spatial integration and decision-support layer connecting observations, process models, data-driven models and management actions. A research agenda is proposed around uncertainty-aware GIS, hybrid physics–AI modelling, cloud-native geospatial workflows, real-time sensor integration, digital twins, explainable AI and reproducible open science. The review provides a conceptual basis for researchers and practitioners to design more transparent, validated and decision-oriented GIS applications in water-resource engineering.

papers.title: Stochastic Operator Residual Learning with Conformal Calibration for Risk-Aware Wind Turbine Maintenance
papers.abstract: Wind turbine maintenance decisions are frequently made under uncertainty, yet conventional degradation models often provide deterministic predictions that ignore the tail risks associated with unexpected component failure. We propose a stochastic operator residual learning framework with conformal calibration for risk-aware wind turbine maintenance. The proposed method learns a distribution over the residual field of governing fatigue and wear equations, rather than enforcing fixed physical laws through penalty terms, so that complex loading spectra and material heterogeneities can be captured without relying on potentially inaccurate constants. An ensemble of neural operators is then trained to separate epistemic from aleatoric uncertainty, and conformal prediction is applied to calibrate the resulting confidence intervals, yielding a remaining useful life distribution with guaranteed coverage. These calibrated distributions are subsequently passed to a risk-sensitive deep reinforcement learning agent whose objective combines power production gains, maintenance costs, and a conditional value-at-risk penalty on the remaining useful life. Furthermore, gradients from the policy update flow back through the calibration layer and the stochastic operator, which allows the uncertainty representation to be shaped by the risk profile required by the controller. The main contribution is a differentiable integration of stochastic residual learning, calibrated uncertainty quantification, and risk-constrained control within a single digital twin architecture. Simulation-based evaluation on representative turbine degradation scenarios will assess whether the framework reduces unexpected failures while preserving energy yield, and the results are expected to inform safer maintenance scheduling under uncertain operating conditions.

This paper proposes a hierarchical planning framework using probabilistic scenario forecasting, two‐stage stochastic programming, and model predictive control (MPC). Day‐ahead bidding optimizes demand response (DR) capacity and resource schedules using two‐stage stochastic programming under behavior uncertainty, while real‐time MPC ensures commitment fulfillment. By explicitly linking scenario‐based bidding with receding‐horizon control, the framework increases bidding aggressiveness without compromising EV charging and hot‐water availability. papers.title: Real-Time Neural Model Predictive Control for Quadrotors via Input-Convex Temporal Convolutional Networks
papers.abstract: Accurate dynamics models are essential for improving the tracking performance of model predictive control (MPC) for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV). However, UAV dynamics are highly nonlinear, strongly coupled, and affected by aerodynamic effects with temporal dependence, which are difficult to capture using nominal rigid-body models alone. For this reason, temporal neural networks (TCNs) have been widely used to learn residual dynamics. Nevertheless, repeated evaluation of network outputs and sensitivities during online optimization incurs substantial computational overhead, hindering real-time implementation. Moreover, integrating temporal residual models into real-time MPC requires causally consistent feature histories at future shooting nodes and efficient horizonwise differentiation. To address these issues, this paper proposes a real-time neural MPC framework that integrates an input-convex TCN residual model, history-conditionedbatched local linearization, and real-time iteration sequential quadratic programming (RTI-SQP).The proposed input-convex temporal convolutional network (IC-TCN) employs causal dilated convolutions and sign-symmetric feature lifting to represent history-dependent residuals in linear andangular accelerations. Under the stated nonnegative-weight and structural constraints, each network output is convex with respect to the complete normalized and lifted causal feature history,which provides a structured residual model for online optimization. Furthermore, to reduce repeated neural-network evaluations over the prediction horizon, the history-conditioned networkoutputs and their current-node first-order sensitivities along the warm-start prediction trajectoryare computed in parallel on a GPU at each sampling instant. The resulting local affine models arethen passed to the RTI-SQP solver, thereby avoiding repeated evaluation of the complete temporalnetwork during the feedback phase and effectively decoupling neural-model computation from online optimization. Simulations with aerodynamic model mismatch and external-force disturbancesshow that, in the tested high-speed scenarios, IC-TCN achieves lower tracking errors than a standard TCN. In addition, on the reported desktop CPUGPU platform, the IC-TCN reduces thedata-driven preparation latency by 39.88% relative to the larger standard TCN.

papers.title: On real-time calibrated prediction for complex model-based decision support in pandemics: Part 1
papers.abstract: Infectious disease models are used to predict the spread and impact of outbreaks of a disease. Like other complex models, they have parameters that need to be calibrated, and structural discrepancies from the reality that they simulate that should be accounted for in calibration and prediction. Whilst Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) techniques have been applied to infectious disease models before, they were not routinely used to inform policymakers in the UK during the COVID-19 pandemic. In this paper, we will argue that during a fast moving pandemic, models and policy are changing on timescales that make traditional UQ methods impractical, if not impossible to implement. We present an alternative formulation to the calibration problem that embeds model discrepancy within the structure of the model, and appropriately assimilates data within the simulation. We then show how UQ can be used to calibrate the model in real-time to produce disease trajectories accounting for parameter uncertainty and model discrepancy. We apply these ideas to an age-structured COVID-19 model for England and demonstrate the types of information it could have produced to feed into policy support prior to the lockdown of March 2020.

papers.title: Hemiarthroplasty with a long femoral stem and proximal cement augmentation for a myeloma-related pathological femoral neck fracture: a case report
papers.abstract: Background Pathological femoral neck fractures are a frequent skeletal complication of multiple myeloma due to extensive osteolytic bone destruction. However, extensive proximal femoral invasion with massive cavitary destruction leading to femoral neck fracture is clinically uncommon, and optimal surgical management remains challenging because of poor bone quality and high mechanical failure risk. Case presentation We report a patient with a known history of multiple myeloma who sustained a low-energy fall resulting in a pathological fracture of the right femoral neck. Imaging demonstrated diffuse osteolytic involvement of the pelvis and proximal femur with severe osteoporosis and degenerative hip changes. Given the patient's poor general condition and multiple comorbidities, a multidisciplinary team (MDT) discussion involving orthopaedics, hematology, cardiology, endocrinology, and neurology was conducted to formulate an individualized perioperative strategy. Bipolar hemiarthroplasty was performed using a long femoral stem with distal press-fit fixation, combined with debridement of tumor-infiltrated tissue, proximal cement augmentation of osteolytic bone defects, and supplemental plate and cerclage cable fixation. This reconstructive strategy was selected as an alternative to proximal femoral replacement to achieve immediate mechanical stability and facilitate early mobilization. Intraoperative autologous blood salvage and reinfusion were used as part of the perioperative blood-management strategy, with no immediate procedure-related complications observed. Results The patient was followed for 15 months after surgery. At the latest follow-up, she remained ambulatory with satisfactory hip function and a Harris Hip Score of 84 points. Follow-up radiographs demonstrated stable reconstruction without prosthetic loosening, dislocation, periprosthetic fracture, or other major implant-related complications. Conclusion Hemiarthroplasty with a long femoral stem, proximal cement augmentation, and supplemental fixation may represent a viable option for selected patients with multiple myeloma-related pathological femoral neck fractures and extensive osteolytic destruction. Careful assessment of bone loss and individualized multidisciplinary planning are important for balancing mechanical stability and perioperative risk.

papers.title: Ultra-broadband mid-infrared plasmonic sensor based on soft-glass photonic crystal fiber for refractive index and temperature detection
papers.abstract: Abstract We introduce a new plasmonic sensor employing a soft-glass photonic crystal fiber configuration for ultra-broadband high-sensitivity refractive index and temperature detection. The analyte channel contains one gold nanowire for plasmonic excitation. A thorough analysis of the sensing characteristics is numerically studied, and the simulation findings indicate that a squeezing lattice structure with one gold nanowire can significantly strengthen the interaction between the y -polarized core mode and surface plasmon polaritons mode across the mid-infrared (MIR) wavelength, leading to complete mode coupling and better detection performance. Through structural optimization, the sensor can achieve single-resonance sensing over the MIR wavelength range of 3.3–5.3 μ m for the analyte RI varying in an ultra-broad range of 1.26–1.50. A peak sensitivity of −18 400 nm RIU −1 coupled with a high RI resolution of −5.43 × 10 −6 RIU is obtained, alongside an average sensitivity of −6766.2 nm RIU −1 demonstrating high linearity (0.9968). Additionally, temperature detection from −60 to 40 °C is realized within 3.0–3.7 μ m wavelengths, achieving a maximum temperature sensitivity of 7.4 nm °C −1 , average sensitivity of 6.7878 nm °C −1 , and linearity coefficient of 0.9989. Owing to its exceptional performance, this sensor offers broad application potential in environmental monitoring, medical diagnostics, chemical analysis, and industrial safety.

papers.title: Layer-Wise Evaluation of Hierarchical Distributed Control for Hybrid Alternating-Current and Direct-Current Microgrid Clusters Under Packet Loss and Forecast Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Hybrid alternating-current/direct-current (AC/DC) microgrid clusters require coordinated battery use, reliable restoration, and economic scheduling under communication and forecast disturbances. This study evaluates a three-layer distributed architecture in a constructed three-microgrid system using public load, solar, and price data from the California Independent System Operator (CAISO). The primary layer combines energy ratings and state of charge (SOC) for discharge sharing. The secondary layer models zero-order-hold (ZOH) receiver memory and tests mean-square stability under independent and identically distributed (IID) packet losses. The tertiary layer uses the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) for distributed model predictive control (DMPC) with forecast correction and matched initial and terminal battery inventories across benchmark methods. On the selected stress day, compared with a grid-only baseline, operating cost and peak grid import decrease by 11.65% and 3.30%, respectively, while imported energy increases by 1.31%. The realized-cost difference from the centralized reference is 0.0029%. Supplementary tests examine longer discharge periods, complete communication outages, and reduced-order cross-layer behavior. Persistent-load-step tests reveal a restoration limitation of the original secondary controller. An integral candidate restores the tested deviations under combined disturbances. These findings characterize layer-specific performance and limited cross-layer responses within tested models. Field readiness and seasonal generalization remain unverified.

papers.title: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control of Process Water Quality in the Closed-Loop Water Circuit of the Aktogai GOK Flotation Plant
papers.abstract: This paper presents a simulation-based feasibility study of nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) for process water quality management in the closed-loop water circuit of the Aktogai copper concentrator. Repeated water recirculation leads to the accumulation of total dissolved solids (TDSs), organic compounds (CODs), and suspended solids (TSSs), degrading flotation efficiency. A dynamic model of the process water pond with nine flows is combined with pseudo-first-order kinetics for H2O2 oxidation (kox = 0.003 L/(mg·h)) and polyaluminum chloride (PAC)/FeCl3 coagulation (kcoag = 0.005 L/(mg·h)). The NMPC manipulates the treated-effluent flow Q2 and the coagulant and oxidant doses over an 8 h prediction horizon, uses normalized one-sided soft constraints on water quality and a reagent cost, and is solved through sequential quadratic programming. The volume, TDSs, and TSSs are assumed to be measured online, whereas CODs are available only from laboratory analyses taken every 2–8 h with a 2 h delay. NMPC was compared with no-control, fixed dosing, a maximum-dilution policy, and a proportional–integral (PI) feedback dosing benchmark with the same manipulated variables. Under nominal disturbances, all strategies met the process limits. Under a simulated stress-test scenario (ore change and reagent overdosing), no control produced 26, 37, and 25 h of TDS, COD, and TSS violations in 72 h; maximum dilution alone removed the TDS and TSS violations but left 13 h of COD violations. With online measurements, a well-tuned PI controller performed almost as well as NMPC (1 h vs. 0 h of COD violations). With laboratory COD analyses, the PI controller incurred 4–11 h of COD violations, whereas NMPC, using a model-based COD estimate between analyses, incurred none, at the cost of 9–47% higher oxidant consumption; this advantage reflects the combined effect of model-based COD estimation and predictive optimization, not of predictive optimization alone. It persisted under up to 30% adverse parametric plant–model mismatch, and the results were insensitive to tenfold variations in the selected NMPC tuning weights. TDSs could be held below their limit only through hydraulic dilution and only while the thickener-overflow TDSs remained below about 2260 mg/L.

papers.title: 3D Corneal and Retinal Bioprinting: Tissue Engineering Strategies, Translational Challenges, and Clinical Opportunities.
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting has emerged as a promising strategy for addressing major unmet needs in ophthalmology, including the global shortage of donor corneal tissue and the absence of restorative therapies for retinal degenerative disease. Advances in biomaterials, stem cell biology, and biofabrication have enabled increasingly sophisticated ocular constructs, ranging from engineered corneal grafts to multicellular retinal models that recapitulate key aspects of native tissue architecture. However, substantial challenges remain in reproducing the optical, mechanical, and biological functions required for clinical translation. This review critically evaluates the current state of corneal and retinal bioprinting through a framework organized around tissue target, fabrication modality, and intended application. Major bioprinting approaches, including extrusion-based, laser-assisted, drop-on-demand, and light-based technologies, are compared with respect to resolution, cell compatibility, scalability, and translational potential. Particular emphasis is placed on the engineering constraints governing construct fidelity, bioink design, tissue integration, and long-term functional performance. Current evidence suggests that corneal and retinal bioprinting have progressed along distinct translational trajectories. Corneal bioprinting has achieved encouraging preclinical outcomes, with selected approaches entering early clinical evaluation, whereas retinal bioprinting has generated highly informative disease models but remains at an earlier stage of translational development. Across both tissues, the field has increasingly shifted from reproducing individual cellular components toward reconstructing the biological interfaces and multicellular systems that underlie tissue function. Future progress will depend on establishing functional validation frameworks, reproducible manufacturing workflows, and standardized benchmarks to support the clinical development of vision-restoring bioprinted constructs.
